h1:
Krabi Street Food & Markets
Where to Eat
intro: Krabi isn't just sea and limestone cliffs. Get up a little early and walk into the Maharaj fresh market, and you'll find the real southern Thai food that locals eat every day. Come Friday to Sunday evening, the Soi Maharaj 8 walking street opens, and if you're staying over in Ao Nang there's a beachside night market to graze through every night. We've rounded up the spots that are actually open, with what's good and rough prices to go with it.

blocks.html: The charm of eating in Krabi is in the markets, not the fancy restaurants. Mornings are when the Maharaj fresh market is busiest, packed with vendors and locals doing their grocery shopping. At night the action shifts to the walking street downtown and the beachside market in Ao Nang. This article makes it clear which market is open on which day, at what hours, and what you should eat there.

blocks.text: Maharaj Fresh Market — Krabi locals' real breakfast

blocks.html: The Maharaj fresh market (on Maharaj Road in downtown Krabi) is the largest fresh market in the province. It opens around 4am, but the busiest stretch with the fullest spread of food is 6:00–9:00am. The front of the market and the streets around it have rows of ready-to-eat stalls — perfect if you want a southern-style breakfast before heading out on an island trip or over to Ao Nang.

items.name: Dim sum baskets
items.blurb: Like a lot of southern Thai towns, Krabi is a dim sum town. Pork dumplings, har gow, and barbecue-pork buns steamed hot in bamboo baskets — order them piece by piece and pair them with old-school filter coffee or hot tea for a proper southern breakfast.

items.name: Pork & shredded-chicken congee
items.blurb: Thick congee with minced pork and a poached egg, topped with shredded ginger and spring onion — a warm-the-belly start before heading out on the boat. Some stalls offer a shredded-chicken version too.

items.name: Roti with curry dip
items.blurb: Roti that's crisp outside and soft inside, dipped in curry (green curry or massaman). It's a Muslim breakfast that's easy to find in Krabi, since the province has a large Muslim community.

items.name: Khao yam (southern rice salad)
items.blurb: Rice tossed with shredded vegetables, toasted coconut, and ground dried shrimp, then drizzled with a well-rounded budu (fermented fish) sauce. A healthy plate that's a southern Thai breakfast signature, and Krabi has its own take on it.

items.name: Khao man gai (chicken rice)
items.blurb: Fragrant rice cooked in chicken fat with boiled or fried chicken, served with a punchy fermented-soybean dipping sauce. A heavier breakfast for days when you've got a long way to travel.

items.name: Khanom jeen nam ya
items.blurb: Rice noodles in a bold, spicy southern nam ya curry, eaten with fresh raw vegetables you serve yourself as much as you like. A classic breakfast that southern families eat in every household.

items.name: Old-school coffee & Thai iced tea
items.blurb: Cap off breakfast with strong sock-brewed coffee or sweet, creamy Thai iced tea, a few baht a cup. Order it to go in a bag and keep sipping as you walk.

blocks.title: Morning market tip
blocks.html: The good stuff at Maharaj market sells out fast. If you want the full spread while it's fresh, getting there before 8am is best. Bring cash and small notes, since most stalls don't take QR payments.

The Krabi walking street is on Soi Maharaj 8 downtown, open only on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from around 5:00–10:00pm. There are more than 70 stalls of food, goods, and souvenirs. The middle of the street has a seating area with a live music stage and performances, and the atmosphere is still local — residents come out to walk it as much as tourists do.

items: Mochi, oyster omelette & pad thai cooked fresh — fried and stir-fried dishes made right in front of you, all smoke and flame and the smell drifting down the whole lane
Hat Yai fried chicken · grilled pork skewers — popular snacks, with pork skewers around 10–20 baht each to eat as you wander
Banana–Nutella roti — sweet roti made fresh with banana, chocolate, or a savoury egg-and-cheese version too
Grilled seafood — charcoal-grilled prawns, squid, and cuttlefish with seafood dipping sauce, priced by size
Mango sticky rice & Thai sweets — to finish, plus khanom krok and brightly coloured Thai sweets

blocks.title: How much budget is enough
blocks.html: Most things at the Krabi walking street run 20–100 baht per item. To really graze your way through, a couple of hundred-baht notes will fill you up easily. Go early in the evening (around 6:00–7:00pm) when the crowd is thinner and everything's still in stock.

blocks.text: Ao Nang Night Market — for those staying beachside

blocks.html: If you're staying in the Ao Nang area you don't need to head into town, because there's the Ao Nang Night Market Landmark (in the Nopparat Thara beach zone, near the pier), open daily, around 4:00pm–10:00/11:00pm. It has over 100 food and drink stalls, leaning toward seafood, Thai food, pizza, and international dishes to suit tourists. There's an open-air seating area, a live music stage, and on some nights Muay Thai and fire shows.

Prices at the Ao Nang market run a little higher than the markets in town since it's a tourist zone, but it's still cheaper than the sit-down restaurants right on the beach. If you want fresh seafood weighed by the kilo and grilled for you, there are several vendors to choose from here — compare prices before you order and you'll come out ahead.

blocks.text: Chao Fa Pier night market + other grazing spots

items.name: Chao Fa Pier night market
items.blurb: On Kongka Road near the Chao Fa pier, open daily from morning to evening. Full range of food — seafood, curries, grilled dishes, roti — around 35–100 baht. Handy to stop by before or after a boat trip.

items.name: Riverside market — black crab statue
items.blurb: Along the Krabi riverfront near the giant black crab statue, with restaurants and food stalls and a local feel. An easy place for an evening stroll by the water.

items.name: Railay walking street
items.blurb: At the entrance to Railay West beach, about 70 metres long, with kebabs, fruit smoothies, burgers, and pancakes for anyone over for a swim or some climbing.

faq.q: Where is the best morning market in Krabi?
faq.a: The Maharaj fresh market on Maharaj Road in downtown Krabi is the largest fresh market in the province. It opens around 4am and is busiest from 6:00–9:00am, with a full southern breakfast spread — dim sum, congee, khao yam, and roti with curry dip.

faq.q: What days and hours is the Krabi walking street open?
faq.a: The Krabi walking street is on Soi Maharaj 8 downtown, open only on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from around 5:00–10:00pm, with over 70 food stalls and a live music stage.

faq.q: Roughly how much does food at the Krabi markets cost?
faq.a: Stall snacks start at 10–30 baht, while plated dishes run around 35–100 baht. To really graze, a couple of hundred-baht notes will fill you up. Most stalls take cash, so bring small notes.

faq.q: Is there a market to eat at if I'm staying in Ao Nang?
faq.a: Yes — the Ao Nang Night Market Landmark in the Nopparat Thara beach zone near the pier, open daily around 4:00–10:00pm. It has over 100 food and drink stalls, leaning toward seafood and Thai food, so you can graze without heading into town.

faq.q: Can I pay by QR scan at the Krabi markets?
faq.a: Some stalls take QR payments, but the small stalls in the fresh market and on the walking street still mostly run on cash. We'd recommend keeping cash and small notes on hand.
